desc:
Encoding. A singly linked list with n nodes is given by two arrays. The nodes are numbered 0..n-1; node 0 is the head, vals[i] is the value stored in node i and succ[i] is the number of the node after node i, or -1 if there is none. The node numbers say nothing about the order in the list: follow succ to find it.

The list has no cycle and contains all n nodes. You may delete at most one node from the list (the remaining nodes keep their order). Return true if the values of the remaining list read the same from head to tail as from tail to head, and false otherwise.

Example: the list 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 2 -> 9 -> 1 becomes the palindrome 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 2 -> 1 after deleting the node with value 9, so the answer is true. The list 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 cannot be fixed with one deletion: the answer is false.
constraints: The list starting at node 0 visits all n nodes and ends at a node with succ = -1
hints: Trying every deletion and checking the result for being a palindrome costs O(n<sup>2</sup>). Can you find out where the first problem is?
A list can only be read forward, but you can copy its values into an array in one pass. Then compare from both ends with two indices i and j.
Move i and j inwards while the values are equal. At the first mismatch the deleted node must be at i or at j: check whether the range i+1..j or the range i..j-1 is a palindrome.
editorial: Walk the list once and store the values in an array. Compare from the outside in with two indices. If no mismatch ever appears, the list is already a palindrome and deleting nothing is allowed.

At the first mismatch a[i] != a[j] every pair outside it matches, and any valid deletion must remove one of the two mismatching nodes (deleting any other node leaves the pair a[i], a[j] facing each other or shifts a different element against one of them, but the outer pairs all match, so the mismatch would remain). So the answer is true exactly when the values of i+1..j or those of i..j-1 form a palindrome; each check is a linear scan.
Total time is O(n) and the extra space is O(n) for the array copy.
